_comment: R8.1. Every trainer battle in the chapter, as data. Spec §12 sizes what this table has to carry -- roughly 12-17 battles (3 Lower Meadows trainers, 2-3 in the relay station, 3 regional captains, 2-4 in the stronghold, 2-4 optional patrols) -- so a new trainer is an entry here, never a new script. `scripts/world/trainer_npc.gd` places them and `scripts/combat/encounter_director.gd` fights them.
_comment_defeat_flag: SB9 (autoload/progression_state.gd), the same flat flag store the road gate, the TM pickups and Tam's handover already write to. Set by the encounter director the moment the trainer's last creature faints. It is what makes the battle unrepeatable (`rechallenge: false`), what SC14's bridge will read, and what SC15's reward is recorded against so beating a trainer twice pays once.
_comment_rechallenge: false everywhere for now, and spec §11/§17 is why: a re-fightable trainer is an XP faucet, and grinding is supposed to mean 'play more of the game', not 'replay one fight'. The field exists because a later sparring partner may legitimately want it -- it is not a promise that one does.
_comment_team: Fought SEQUENTIALLY: the trainer sends out the next creature when one faints, in this order. `level` is the creature's real level (D30 arithmetic, data/config/progression.json), NOT a difficulty band. `moves` is optional and overrides the species' own quick/charged pair (data/creatures/species.json) -- for a trainer whose lesson is a specific move, SC13's Tam being the obvious case.
_comment_reward: SC15's shape (spec Sec17 P1 step 9; D39: 'SC15's trainer payouts later pay coins too'). ALL TUNABLE. `coins` (int, default 0) is granted through the ordinary satchel -- `coin` is just another items.json entry (D39), so this is `inventory.add('coin', coins)`, nothing more. `items` are real item ids granted once, each `{id, count}`. `flags` are extra progression flags to set alongside the defeat flag (SC14's South Bridge Key is a flag AND an item). `xp_bonus` (int, default 0, optional) is a FLAT bonus on top of the fight's own per-kill XP -- ordinary victory XP already happens naturally, per creature felled, through combat_manager's award; this is the authored extra, applied flatly (no party-share split, unlike the per-kill award) to every non-fainted party member. Every field pays out only when the defeat flag was NOT already set, so a rechallenge can never pay twice.
_comment_art: `config_key` names a block in data/config/art.json; `rank` instead names a Team Tether rank in data/config/npc_ranks.json (SE25's relay trainers, SF34's captains). Optional `hair`/`palette`/`accessories` are laid over that base -- per-part variants, never one global tint (CLAUDE.md, spec §21). No new human generations here.
_comment_levels_sh47: SH47/D42, the gauntlet. WAS patrol 17/18, courtyard 18/19/19, elite 21/22/22; NOW 15/16, 16/17/17, 18/19/19. TUNABLE, and no fight is removed or added. Two reasons, both measured with tools/_probe_pacing.py. First, the ladder ran the wrong way at the top: the elite's aces were 21 and 22 while the Warden's own ace -- the chapter's boss, the fight everything else prepares for -- is 20. A gauntlet harder than the boss it guards inverts spec Sec8's whole shape. Second, the three regional captains cap at 16, so a player arriving off the Sigil gate faced a five-level step and the probe showed the cost: seven forced wild fights against level-2-to-6 field creatures purely to inflate a number, which is Sec11's `bad grind` by name. The gauntlet now climbs 15 -> 19 across three fights and hands the player to a Warden whose last creature is still the highest level in the chapter. Nothing about the ROOM sequence, the rewards or the rank ladder moved -- only the numbers on the teams.
_comment_positions: World metres [x, z]; Y is always asked of the world (D09). `facing_deg` is the yaw the trainer is placed with; npc_body.gd turns them to face the player on approach regardless.
_comment_placed_by: SC12/SC13. An entry naming `placed_by` is a trainer whose body already exists somewhere else -- `scripts/world/trainer_npc.gd::build()` skips it rather than standing up a second, duplicate body. Mira, Oskar and Tam all name `"village_npcs"`: they are the three existing village NPCs (data/config/village_npcs.json, placed by scripts/world/village_npcs.gd) and spec sec3 Band 1 says outright to reuse them rather than add a fourth. `position`/`facing_deg` below still mirror their real village_npcs.json entry for anyone reading this table, even though nothing spawns from them. Their challenge is offered through village_npcs.gd's own `greeting_when` list (not this file's prompt system) and their fight is started by sequence_director.gd's `battle:<trainer_id>` dialogue effect (not `_on_challenged`/`_on_conversation_finished` below) -- but this table, and `encounter_director.begin_trainer_battle()`, are exactly what both routes read and run.

flow._comment: ALL TUNABLE. `send_out_seconds` is the beat between one of the trainer's creatures fainting and the next stepping up -- long enough to read as them making a decision, short enough that it is not a loading pause. `linger_seconds` is how long a fallen creature stays on the ground before its body is cleared, matching catching.json's own faint linger.

prompts._comment: Built here rather than in code so a trainer can be challenged in words that suit them later. `%s` is the trainer's display name. Never contains "talk" or "choose": tests/smoke_opening.gd finds Grandpa and the starters by exactly those substrings.

trainers.name: Bryn
trainers._placeholder: SC12/SC13 replaced R8.1's placeholder role with Mira, Oskar and Tam below (villager-greeting trainers, `placed_by: "village_npcs"`) -- but this entry stays. tests/smoke_trainer_battle.gd is the ONE test that drives a trainer through trainer_npc.gd's OWN placement-and-prompt system end to end (a real Terrain3D body, a real 'Challenge Bryn' prompt, a real interact-button press) rather than through a villager's greeting_when/battle: route, and there is no other standalone trainer in the game yet for it to stand up. Deleting Bryn would delete that coverage, not just a placeholder -- so it is kept, and noted here rather than silently left behind. A future standalone trainer (the relay station's, a captain's) can take over this exact role later.

hair._comment: Spec §21 and the owner's own playtest note: villagers differ primarily by hair colour. Distinct from farmer (#5c3a22), smith (#8a8578) and ranger (#7a3c22) so a second body on the same base does not read as one of them wandered off.

trainers._why_here: The open north field behind the village square -- inside the square's own 22m vegetation clearing (extended in data/config/vegetation.json so the 11m arena is not fought through a tree), 12m clear of every structure, villager, harvest node and prop, and well outside the bramblebun cluster at [30,-40] so a wild engage prompt never contests the challenge prompt.

trainers.name: Mira
trainers._comment: SC12/SC13. Spec sec3 Band 1: 'Mira -- Meadow Keeper -- introductory trainer battle, reward: XP + useful early item/TM/recipe.' The introduction -- one creature, low level, a coin purse and a potion. Team level is TUNABLE and this task's to set; SC15 owns the payout table's final numbers.

trainers.name: Oskar
trainers._comment: SC12/SC13/SC14. Spec sec3 Band 1: 'Oskar -- Bridgehand -- moderate trainer battle, controls or possesses the old bridge mechanism, reward: South Bridge Key.' The gate -- a real two-creature team, sturdier than Mira's. `south_bridge_key` is SC14's Gate 1 mechanism; this entry hands it over the moment it is defeated so the bridge task has a real item to read rather than a stub.

trainers.name: Tam
trainers._comment: SC12/SC13. Spec sec3 Band 1: 'Tam -- Field Scout -- battle emphasizing switching/type awareness, reward: TM, Orb-related item, or map hint.' The switching lesson -- two creatures of different types, so a one-note team cannot answer both.

trainers.name: Hess
trainers._comment: SE25. Spec sec3 Band 3 / sec12: 'two or three Team Tether trainers and a relay captain' at the relay station. The OUTER picket -- the first Team Tether personnel the player is ever stopped by, met on the approach road well before the site itself. Levels are Band 3 (~8-12) and ALL TUNABLE; never player-scaled (spec sec11/D30: a level is a real level, and the world does not move to meet you).
trainers._site: SE23 IS NOT BUILT YET. These four stand at the relay SITE, whose one authored coordinate is data/config/relay_site.json's `site.centre` [108, 34] -- on the quarry's own conduit bearing toward the stronghold (old_quarry.json's [229.8,-144.4]), 150m out from the quarry floor. Every position below is derived from that centre. When SE23 builds the station it should ADOPT relay_site.json's centre rather than pick another, and move these four with it if it needs to.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: moved by the same uniform (+242,+3726) offset as relay_site.json's `site.centre` (108,34)->(350,3760). Pure translation, so `facing_deg` (-34.4, == `approach_bearing_deg`) is still correct without re-deriving it.
trainers._why_here: On the approach, 22m short of the site centre, facing back down the conduit road the player walks up. Ground here measures -5.55m with 1.84m of spread over an 8m box (tools/_probe_relay.gd) -- gentle enough for an 11m arena.

trainers.name: Orrin
trainers._comment: SE25. The INNER picket -- the second stop on the same road, a little stronger and a little further in. Two grunts before an officer before the captain is the rank ladder NP2's palettes exist to make readable at gameplay distance.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same (+242,+3726) offset as relay_site.json's `site.centre`.
trainers._why_here: 13m short of the site centre on the same bearing. Ground -4.31m, 1.95m spread over an 8m box.

trainers.name: Officer Dell
trainers._comment: SE25. The relay's own duty officer, standing on the site itself rather than out on the road -- three creatures where the pickets field two, and the first of the four whose badge is bronze rather than grey.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same (+242,+3726) offset as relay_site.json's `site.centre`.
trainers._why_here: On the site's south-west edge, 4m out from centre. Ground -3.37m, 1.53m spread.

trainers.name: Captain Vance
trainers._comment: SE25. The relay captain, and the fight SE27 is waiting on. `rank: captain` puts him a full step above Dell's bronze and a full step below the Warden's crimson on NP2's badge ladder -- spec sec36's rank read, made at a glance rather than in a title card. Three creatures, the highest levels in the chapter so far (11-12, TUNABLE), and the only reward in the table carrying an xp_bonus: this is the end of a four-battle site, not a roadside challenge.
trainers._authority_not_menace: See data/dialogue/trainers.json for the lines. He is the most articulate of the four; Tether personnel believe the barriers are necessary work and that the player is interfering with it.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same (+242,+3726) offset as relay_site.json's `site.centre`.
trainers._why_here: At the console end of the site, 3.6m past centre on the bearing, so he is between the player and the captive -- the fight cannot be walked around. Ground -2.31m, 1.05m spread.
trainers._comment_defeat_flag: SE27 waits on exactly this id. data/config/relay_site.json gates the captive's rescue conversation on it, and nothing else in the chapter sets it.

trainers.name: Patrolman Verrick
trainers._comment: SG38, spec Sec8 'Outer Works: patrol trainer'. The first Team Tether body the player meets inside the stronghold's own works, and the lowest rank on Sec36's ladder -- a grunt on a walk, not a gatekeeper. Two creatures, both a little above the captains' band: this fight's job is to tell an under-levelled party to turn around while turning around is still cheap.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: same (-141.8,+7775.4) offset as stronghold.json's `site.at` (141.8,-215.4)->(0,7560), since this fallback mirrors the room's own (translation-only) position.
trainers._position_note: FALLBACK ONLY. scripts/world/stronghold.gd places this row from data/config/stronghold.json's `gauntlet` block, because the coordinates of a spot inside a room belong to the room. This is the same point, written out so the row still stands somewhere sane if the building ever fails to build.

trainers.name: Warder Solene
trainers._comment: SG38, spec Sec8 'Courtyard / Hall Approach: trainer fight'. An officer on Sec36's ladder, and the first three-creature team in the building -- the step up from the patrol is a whole extra creature, not just levels, because that is what actually punishes a party of two.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same offset as stronghold_patrol above.

trainers.name: Keeper Hald
trainers._comment: SG38, spec Sec8 'Tether Chamber Approach: elite trainer'. Captain rank, three creatures of three different types, and the hardest fight before the Warden. His defeat flag is also the ONE door in the complex: data/config/stronghold.json's tether_approach->warden_arena passage is `gated_by_flag: defeated_stronghold_elite`, so he is not a fight the player can walk around. The recovery point sits behind him, which is the order Sec8 asks for -- elite, then rest, then the Warden.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same offset as stronghold_patrol above.

trainers.name: Captain Halder
trainers._comment: SF34, spec §3 Band 4. The first of the three regional captains: Ground-focused team, rewards the Field Sigil. Team levels are TUNABLE and sit inside §3's own 'roughly 10-16 entering this band' -- NEVER player-scaled (§3 says so outright): a player who over-levels walks through him, and that is the reward for over-levelling.
trainers._comment_palette: NP2's CAPTAIN rank palette (#b0a271, data/config/npc_ranks.json) with ONE regional accent -- a half-step toward the dry straw of the high pasture. Per CLAUDE.md and spec §21 this is a per-material variant laid over the rank base, not a new mesh and not a global tint; `character_model.gd` applies `rank` first and this over it, so all three captains still read as the same rank at a glance and differ by posting.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: this captain was 'unplaced/near village' (the (52,-122) below was a Band-4-shaped stand-in on the OLD map, not a real Band 4 site -- the old map had no Band 4). Moved to (170,5590), the position section 3.1's Band 4 waypoint list names explicitly for the Field Captain. `facing_deg` (-20.6) is UNCHANGED and is almost certainly wrong for the new site -- it was derived by atan2 back to the OLD village at roughly the origin, and the new corridor's Band 4 geometry is a different shape entirely. Left as a flag rather than invented: re-deriving a correct facing needs the reviewer to pick which way 'back down the road' points on the new spine, which is authoring judgement past a coordinate relocation.
trainers._why_here: The high pasture west of the Rise, on the trainer road up-country (spec Band 4's 'high pasture' and 'trainer road'). MEASURED, not guessed: `tools/_probe_upper_meadows.gd` reads h=0.59m, 0.64m of height spread and a worst local slope of 6.0 degrees over an 8m pad -- a real arena, on the flattest ground in the upper Meadows. 28.6m clear of the Burrow Warrens' mouth at [70,-140] so the dungeon's own prompt never contests the challenge, 133m from the origin and well inside world_perimeter.gd's 235m ring. `facing_deg` is the yaw that looks back down the road toward the village, the same atan2(dx, dz) convention every other entry in this file uses. STALE after OW5D's move -- see `_comment_ow5d` above; ground here was not re-probed either.

trainers.name: Captain Vess
trainers._comment: SF34. The second captain: Air-focused team, rewards the Ridge Sigil. A level step above the Field Captain -- the three are meant to be fought in road order, not in one sitting, and nothing enforces that order because nothing needs to: the Sigils are a set and the gate counts them, not their sequence.
trainers._comment_palette: Captain base, accented toward the pale grey-green of the wind ridge -- see captain_field's own note for why this is a per-material accent rather than a tint or a new body.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation to (-280,6460), section 3.1's named 'Ridge Captain' position (watchtower spur). `facing_deg` UNCHANGED and stale -- see captain_field's own OW5D note; the same reasoning applies here.
trainers._why_here: The shoulder under the Rise's south-west face, where the wind ridge starts and the walkable ground ends -- everything east of here measures 43 to 76 degrees of rock in the same probe, so this is literally the last place on the ridge a fight can happen. MEASURED: h=-1.51m, 2.79m spread, worst slope 12.8 degrees over a 9m pad, 168m out. 36m from the Field Captain and 46m from the Riverwatch Captain: three distinct places, none of them in sight-and-prompt range of another. STALE after OW5D's move -- ground not re-probed at the new site.

trainers.name: Captain Oreth
trainers._comment: SF34. The third captain: Water-led but deliberately BALANCED (spec §3 says 'Water/balanced'), so a party built to answer the first two cannot walk this one on type alone -- two Water and one Ground, the only mixed team of the three. Top of the band's tunable 10-16.
trainers._comment_palette: Captain base, accented toward the wet slate of the draw. Same per-material rule as the other two.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation to (-100,4350), section 3.1's own text: 'Riverwatch Captain sits off-spine on the Band 3/4 seam.' `facing_deg` UNCHANGED and stale -- see captain_field's own OW5D note. This captain's whole `_why_here` below describes a posting that watches for a river that, per this same macro-layout document (section 5), now actually exists nearby (the river crosses the corridor at z~4200, per section 10.2's Old Mill Crossing row) -- the 'no actual watercourse here yet' caveat is arguably resolved by the new geography, but confirming that is OW5C's river work, not this pass's.
trainers._why_here: The low draw at the foot of the Rise's south-east flank -- the lowest ground in the upper Meadows (h=-6.54m, 6.9m below the Field Captain's pasture), which is where the ridge's runoff would collect and what a Riverwatch posting is watching. MEASURED: 1.48m spread, worst slope 10.5 degrees over an 8m pad, 209m out. HONEST LIMIT, recorded rather than papered over: there is no actual watercourse here yet -- the Meadows' only running water is the west stream and the pond (terrain_playground.json `water`), and Band 3's river geography is SE22's, not this item's. This is the right SHAPE of ground for the posting and the terrain lease is held elsewhere, so no bake was run to put water in it. If SE22 ever cuts an upper draw, it belongs on this spot. STALE after OW5D's move -- see `_comment_ow5d` above.

trainers.name: Warden Aldis
trainers._comment: R8.3, spec Act VI step 35 and M14 -- the chapter's last fight. THERE IS NO BOSS MODE AND NO BOSS SCRIPT. He is an ordinary row of this same table: the same team schema, the same reward schema, the same defeat flag, the same encounter_director.begin_trainer_battle(), the same sequential send-out, and catching refused exactly as it is refused for every other trainer in the game (a trainer's creatures are theirs -- CLAUDE.md's hard rule). What makes him the boss is the ONLY thing spec sec12 says makes a boss: a full team of five and the highest levels in the chapter.
trainers._comment_character: Spec sec33 gives him a worldview rather than a motive, and the lines are in data/dialogue/stronghold.json. He is not a moustache-twirler: he believes separation prevents chaos and that ordinary people do not understand the risks, he confirms the readout rather than denying it, and he does not recant when he loses. His face is still PAINTED rather than modelled (HANDOFF sec6) -- flagged, not faked. Sec20 covers creatures, so a Warden face sheet is legal under sec22's budget, but it is owner-gated art and no generation was spent here.
trainers._comment_rank: data/config/npc_ranks.json's top tier -- the crimson badge at its largest, on the Warden's own rig. He is the rig every other Team Tether rank in the chapter has been a variant of, met last and unmodified.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same (-141.8,+7775.4) offset as stronghold.json's `site.at`, since this fallback mirrors the room's own (translation-only) position.
trainers._position_note: FALLBACK ONLY, and it mirrors the Warden Arena's own centre-ish point. scripts/world/stronghold_climax.gd places him from the `warden_stand` mark that R8.2's data/config/stronghold.json registers, because a room's coordinates belong to the room. Written out so the row still stands somewhere sane if the building ever fails to build.
trainers._comment_team: A FULL team of five -- the only trainer in the chapter who fields one, and the first time the player's own five-creature limit is met by an equal. Levels 16-20 sit above SF34's captains (10-16) with the ace a clear step above the rest. Three types across the five so no single answer sweeps it: two Ground, one Water, one Air, and a Ground ace. ALL TUNABLE.
trainers._comment_defeat_flag: R8.4 waits on exactly this id: data/config/stronghold_climax.json gates the tether machine shut until it is set, so a player who sprints past him cannot reach the Legendary Chamber's lever with the boss still standing. Spec sec28's order is not optional and this flag is where that is enforced. SG44's world event reads `legendary_freed`, not this.

_comment_stronghold: SG38 (spec Sec8, Sec12). The stronghold gauntlet: a patrol at the Outer Works, a fight in the Courtyard, and an elite in front of the Tether Chamber Approach's door -- three of Sec12's '2-4 final stronghold trainers', with the Warden himself (R8.3) the fourth fight in the building. All three carry `placed_by: "stronghold"`, so trainer_npc.gd's world pass skips them and scripts/world/stronghold.gd places them from the room layout instead. Levels are TUNABLE and never player-scaled (Sec3): they sit above the 10-16 the captains' band expects, which is the whole point of a gauntlet an unprepared party should not clear.
